message: Open bookings on a rolling window and allow longer bookings

findings.summary: `BookingStore.between` returns only bookings that start inside [start, end), so the member check misses a longer booking that started earlier and is still running. A member with 18:00 to 19:30 on Court 1 can also book Court 2 at 19:00. The check needs the same look-back and `b.end > start` filter as the court check above it.

`book` passes `start` in UTC, so `start.date()` is the UTC date. In Sydney a slot before 11:00 (10:00 in winter) falls on the previous UTC date, so its booking opens a day early: on 2 March at 09:00 a full member can book 08:00 on 10 March, which should open on 3 March, while the booking sheet still shows it closed. The date should come from `clock.local(start)`.

`Booking.length` is a count of 30-minute slots, but it is added to `minutes` and compared with `DAILY_MINUTES`. Three hours already booked count as 6, so the 120-minute limit is never reached in practice: a member can book 90 minutes in the morning and 90 more in the evening.

decoys.summary: The look-back of `MAX_MINUTES - SLOT_MINUTES` looks one slot short but is right. Bookings start on slot boundaries, `Booking.end` is exclusive, and `between` includes its start bound, so the earliest booking that can still be running at `start` begins 60 minutes before it, and the `b.end > start` filter drops the rest.

Passing `tzinfo=` to `datetime.combine` gives a wrong local-mean-time offset only with pytz. `CLUB_TZ` is a `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo` (courts/config.py), which resolves the offset for that date, daylight saving included, and `clock.day_bounds` and `slots.day_slots` build club times the same way.

`length=minutes // SLOT_MINUTES` looks like a unit mix-up, but `Booking.length` is a number of slots (courts/models.py), and `Booking.end` multiplies it by `SLOT_MINUTES`. A 90-minute booking is stored with a length of 3, and the court check on the next line gets an end 90 minutes after the start.
